newsitem.title: DUBAI: Bahrain expels German agency reporter for article.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain expels German agency reporter for article.

text.p: Bahrain expelled a German agency reporter for an article which allegedly contained "fallacies and offences" to the country, Bahrain's official Gulf News Agency said on Tuesday.

"An official source at the ministry of cabinet affairs and information said the correspondent of the German news agency DPA (Deutsche Presse Agentur) had been asked to leave the country for publishing a report containing fallacies and offences to the state of Bahrain," the agency said.
DPA said in a story faxed to Reuters in Dubai that its correspondent Ute Meinel had been expelled early on Tuesday for a report she wrote quoting an exiled opposition group.
"The expulsion was criticised by DPA's top editors in Hamburg who called it completely incomprehensible and a violation of the principles of press freedom," DPA said.
"The German Foreign Office in Bonn summoned Bahrain's ambassador so it could express Germany's disagreement with what it called Bahrain's 'harsh reaction'," DPA said.
The story said Meinel had worked in the Gulf Arab state for three years.
Bahrain, the Gulf's financial and banking centre, has for the past two years been the scene of anti-government protests in which more than 25 people have been killed.

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since December 1994 to press the Sunni-led government to implement economic and political reforms.
A series of arson attacks in early June were described by a government official as "continued acts of terrorism".
